title: Genetically Engineered Quantum Circuits for Financial Market Indicators
abstract_summary: This preprint proposes using GASP (Genetic Algorithm for State Preparation) to optimize encoding of stock price data into quantum states, yielding low-depth, low-gate-count circuits with improved fidelity and efficiency. The authors demonstrate encoding on simulated and real quantum hardware and apply a variational quantum SVD (VQSVD) to compute SVD entropy of correlation matrices, showing more accurate singular values and favorable trade-offs between fidelity and resource usage compared with qGAN and AAE. They conclude that approximate state preparation via GASP is practical for NISQ-era quantum finance applications.
methodology_description: The authors evaluate the use of a genetic-algorithm-based state preparation method (GASP) to encode real-world stock-price-derived data into low-depth quantum circuits and then extract singular values / SVD entropy via a variational quantum singular value decomposition (VQSVD) routine. Financial data (monthly opening prices) for four stocks were retrieved and converted to logarithmic returns, standardised and normalised to produce a matrix of a_nt values. These a_nt entries were assembled into a normalised bipartite quantum state |data> over a stock index and a time index. GASP was used to generate parameterised quantum circuits that approximately prepare the |data> state at a set of target fidelities (70%–99%). For diagonalisation, shallow variational circuits U(theta) and V(theta') (single layer of Rz and Ry rotations on each qubit plus CNOTs connecting adjacent qubits) were applied to the prepared |data> state to approximate a Schmidt decomposition; a cost LSVD based on two-qubit Pauli-Z correlators (sum of 1 - <σz σz>^2 terms) was minimised with a classical optimiser (reported as SPASA) to align the state to computational-basis-paired Schmidt components. The squared Schmidt coefficients yield singular values and SVD entropy S = -Σ |c_j|^2 ln |c_j|^2. Experiments compared GASP-based preparation to two variational loading baselines (qGAN and AAE), and evaluation metrics included fidelity, singular-value reconstruction distance, Frobenius-norm reconstruction error of the correlation matrix, loss vs iteration traces, and mean-squared error of computed SVD entropy versus the ideal diagonalisation.
algorithms_used: MMD (Maximum Mean Discrepancy) used within AAE

pipeline_steps: 1) Retrieve monthly opening prices for the four stocks from Yahoo Finance.
2) Compute logarithmic returns r_nt and standardise per stock to obtain a_nt following Eq. (3).
3) Build correlation matrix C_nm = Σ_t a_nt a_mt and assemble normalised target quantum state |data> = Σ_{n,t} a_nt |n>|t>.
4) Use GASP to generate approximate state-preparation circuits for |data> at target fidelities (tested targets: 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90%, 95%, 99%).
5) Prepare |data> on the quantum device/simulator using the GASP circuit (or prepare comparators via qGAN and AAE methods).
6) Apply variational QSVD circuits U(theta) and V(theta') (one layer of per-qubit Rz and Ry rotations followed by linear CNOT entangling across qubits) to the prepared state.
7) Evaluate the LSVD cost, LSVD(theta,theta') = Σ_{q=1}^{ns} (1 - <σ_q^z σ_{q+ns}^z> )^2, and update parameters using the reported classical optimiser (SPASA) to minimise cost.
8) After optimisation, read off squared Schmidt coefficients |c_j|^2 as estimated singular values; compute SVD entropy S = -Σ |c_j|^2 ln(|c_j|^2).
9) Compare singular values, reconstructed correlation matrix (Frobenius norm error), and SVD entropy against ideal baseline (direct diagonalisation) and against qGAN/AAE methods.

key_findings: [supported] The GASP (Genetic Algorithm for State Preparation) framework can be used to generate approximate quantum state-preparation circuits that encode stock-price-derived data vectors (correlation-matrix-based 'data' states).

[supported] GASP-generated circuits can achieve high target state fidelities (they report producing circuits targeted at 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90%, 95%, and 99% fidelities) for the 4-qubit demonstrations used in the paper.

[supported] Higher-fidelity GASP circuits produce more accurate singular values and improved reconstruction of the correlation matrix compared with the qGAN and AAE loading methods used for comparison in the study.

[supported] There are diminishing returns in improving the accuracy of the calculated SVD entropy beyond roughly 90% target fidelity; increasing fidelity from ≈90% to 99% yields substantially more resource cost (gates/time) for minimal SVD-entropy accuracy gain.

[supported] GASP-produced circuits tend to have low gate depth and gate count relative to exact-state-synthesis methods, making them more feasible to run on NISQ-era hardware (as argued and empirically demonstrated in small-scale examples).

[supported] Approximate state preparation (via GASP) is sufficient for accurate estimation of SVD entropy in the presented financial-data examples; exact state preparation is not necessary for useful results in that task.

[speculative] The approach (GASP for state preparation + VQSVD) can broadly improve financial analysis tasks such as risk management, asset allocation, and market forecasting when deployed on NISQ-era quantum computers.

[speculative] The paper implies applicability of GASP-generated circuits on 'real quantum computers' (beyond simulation), but explicit, detailed hardware-run results and metrics are not clearly presented in the main text.
[speculative] Using approximate state preparation as a standard trade-off (accuracy vs resource) will materially accelerate practical quantum finance applications on near-term devices.
results_summary: The paper demonstrates that GASP can be used to generate low-depth, approximate quantum state-preparation circuits that encode stock-price-derived data vectors for use in a variational quantum SVD (VQSVD) workflow to compute SVD (von Neumann) entropy from correlation matrices. In 4-qubit demonstrations (4 stocks × 4 time steps) the authors compare GASP-generated loading circuits at a range of target fidelities (70%–99%) against qGAN and AAE loading methods, finding that higher-fidelity GASP circuits yield more accurate singular values and correlation-matrix reconstructions, but that accuracy gains in SVD entropy plateau above ≈90% fidelity while resource costs (gates/time) continue to rise. They conclude that approximate state preparation via GASP offers a favorable accuracy/resource trade-off for NISQ-era financial algorithms.

quantum_advantage_detail: The paper demonstrates more efficient approximate state preparation for a small-scale financial indicator computation and argues this improves feasibility on NISQ devices, but it does not demonstrate a provable or empirical quantum computational advantage (speedup or performance beyond classical methods) for the financial tasks considered. Broader claims about impact on finance are therefore speculative rather than demonstrated.
limitations: Many exact state-preparation methods produce circuits with depths that are infeasible on current hardware (author-stated).
Introducing ancillary qubits can reduce depth but ancilla are limited on current hardware (author-stated).

GASP produces approximate state preparations; achieving very high target fidelities (e.g. 99%) incurs substantially higher time and gate costs with diminishing improvements in SVD-entropy accuracy (author-stated).
Circuits generated by GASP are typically unique due to the stochastic nature of genetic algorithms, leading to variability and potential reproducibility issues (author-stated).

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — GASP (genetic algorithm for state preparation) yields low-depth, low-gate-count circuits that achieve higher fidelity and more accurate singular-value (Schmidt coefficient) reconstruction and SVD entropy estimates than qGAN and AAE baselines on the 4-qubit financial correlation-data examples.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — The approach is demonstrated on both simulators and real quantum hardware (4 qubits, target fidelities 70%–99%), and authors argue approximate state preparation via GASP is practical for NISQ-era finance tasks such as SVD/entropy estimation of small correlation matrices.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The pipeline combines classical genetic optimisation (GASP) for circuit synthesis, shallow variational QSVD circuits (single-layer Rz/Ry + CNOTs) and a classical optimiser (SPASA) to extract singular values and compute SVD entropy.
#limitation:qubit-count — Experiments are limited to 4 qubits (2 stock × 2 time); scalability to larger asset universes or longer time windows is not demonstrated and remains an open question.

#limitation:noise — Real-hardware fidelity targets and trade-offs are discussed, implying noise impacts accuracy; the results depend on approximate preparation fidelities and shallow circuits, so hardware noise remains a limiting factor.

#limitation:data-encoding — While GASP reduces circuit depth/gate counts for state preparation, the work does not quantify costs or scaling of encoding larger, higher-dimensional financial datasets; data-loading overheads remain unresolved.
